subject.title: Import Scrollmark and twitter-web-exporter captures into the canonical local store

question: Should Birdclaw own a versioned third-party capture-import contract now, and if so should the first supported producer be limited to Scrollmark canonical bundle v1?
rationale: Implementation requires a durable policy for external schema compatibility, provenance, collection completeness, account scoping, migrations, and backup preservation that cannot safely be inferred from existing archive behavior.

options.title: Stage Scrollmark v1
options.body: Approve only the versioned Scrollmark canonical bundle for the first implementation and require fixtures plus an explicit provenance and completeness contract before adding other producers.

options.title: Design a generic adapter contract
options.body: Define a producer-neutral capture adapter and versioning API before implementing either Scrollmark or twitter-web-exporter support.

options.title: Defer capture imports
options.body: Keep official archives, live transports, and Birdclaw backups as the supported ingestion boundaries until third-party formats demonstrate longer-term stability.

recommendation.title: Stage Scrollmark v1
recommendation.body: Approve only the versioned Scrollmark canonical bundle for the first implementation and require fixtures plus an explicit provenance and completeness contract before adding other producers.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice affects Birdclaw’s product boundary, canonical storage contract, migrations, and long-term format support.
